title: How to Fix Cell Samples in FlexV2
author: Yujun Feng
materials: PN1000781 GEM-X Flex Sample Preparation v2 Kit
Other reagents to check: PBS (1X) and BSA. Optional: 50% Glycerol, for long-term storage

steps.title: Verify kit availability and storage
steps.instruction: Check that the PN1000781 GEM‑X Flex Sample Preparation v2 Kit is present, note the remaining/used reaction count on the box, and confirm the box is stored on the second shelf at –20 °C in the SGT room with enough reactions for the planned number of cell or nuclei samples.

steps.title: Count cells and assess quality
steps.instruction: Upon receipt of fresh samples, count cells on a cell counter; record viability, total cell number per sample, and debris level. Viability should be >80 % (50‑80 % is acceptable with caution; <50 % requires warning about higher mitochondrial reads). Ensure each sample contains between 200 k and 10 M cells; low numbers risk loss, high numbers risk insufficient fixation. If debris is high, reduce it before fixation (see 10x Genomics KB link).

steps.title: Concentrate cells if needed
steps.instruction: If cell concentration is ≤10⁵ cells / mL, centrifuge to concentrate: default 350 g for 5 min at 4 °C; use 150 g for 5 min at 4 °C for fresh tumor cells. Adjust parameters with the user if a different protocol is required.

steps.title: Pellet cells and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample at 350 g for 5 min at 4 °C for PBMCs/cell lines, or at 150 g for 10 min at 4 °C for dissociated tumor cells. Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet, leaving up to 30 µL behind.

steps.title: Fix cells with Buffer B
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL room‑temperature Fixation Buffer B to the cell pellet and pipette‑mix five times to resuspend.

steps.title: Choose immediate or delayed probe hybridization
steps.instruction: Decide whether to proceed directly to probe hybridization (GEM‑X workflow) or to postpone the step for later processing.

steps.title: Incubate fixation at 20°C then 4°C
steps.instruction: Incubate the fixed sample at 20 °C for 1 hour. If fixation is being delayed, continue incubation at 4 °C for 16–24 hours before proceeding to the “On the day of probe incubation” steps.

steps.title: Add Additive C to fixation mix
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL room‑temperature Additive C to the sample (still in Fixation Buffer) and pipette‑mix five times.

steps.title: Pellet and remove supernatant post‑Additive C
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 850 g for 5 min at room temperature, then remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet (up to 30 µL may be left).

steps.title: Quench fixation with chilled buffer
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL chilled Quenching Buffer to the pellet and mix five times on ice. If the sample contains <100 k cells, first add 200 µL, mix, then add the remaining 800 µL after the counting step.

steps.title: Add Enhancer and store fixed sample
steps.instruction: Thaw Enhancer (PN200482) at 65 °C for 10 min, then add 0.1 × the volume of the fixed sample, pipette‑mix, and store the sample at 4 °C for up to 1 week. After this, continue with the probe‑hybridization workflow as described in the “On the day of probe incubation” section.
